entry.title: Navigating Mental Health Services at Boston University | Just Curious Folks with JCF (Ep. 4)

media:group.media:title: Navigating Mental Health Services at Boston University | Just Curious Folks with JCF (Ep. 4)
media:group.media:description:
In Episode 4 of Just Curious Folks w/JCF, Boston University Dean of Students Jason Campbell-Foster, Ed.D., talks with psychologist Dr. Kara Cattani about student mental health, loneliness, resilience, and how the campus community can help students feel supported and connected.
Dr. Cattani shares practical ways students can manage stress and care for their well-being, from starting with small, realistic steps to building connections with peers. They also discuss how faculty and staff can foster belonging, make room for honest conversations about mental health, and support students without adding to the pressures they already face.
The conversation explores BU mental health resources, including CAPS services and options beyond individual counseling, as well as SARP’s work to promote consent, healthy relationships, and a culture of care. Listen to this episode of Just Curious Folks w/JCF, a Boston University podcast hosted by Jason Campbell-Foster.
CHAPTERS: ____________________________________________ 0:00 — Introduction 0:23 — Dr. Kara Cattani’s path into college mental health 1:49 — Student mental health today: loneliness, anxiety, and AI 4:30 — Individual coping and the campus environment 7:02 — Resilience, stress, and avoiding burnout 9:35 — Practical ways to support well-being 11:39 — How faculty and staff can support students 13:42 — Consent, healthy relationships, and SARP 18:01 — CAPS services and mental health support options 24:02 — BU’s "Let’s Talk About Mental Health" initiative 26:44 — Belonging and small acts of care 31:09 — Closing Takeaways ____________________________________________
